messages:
maya: Quick check — germanium-13b int6 onboard looks great on tokens saved but I'm worried about QA regressions. can we do a short econ vs quality verdict?

ravi: Thanks Maya. what's the delta on unit cost + the measured quality drop?

maya: Short numbers from the slice run:```
fp16 baseline: latency p95 220ms, cost ~ $1.00 / 1M tokens, QA pass@1 78.4
int8: latency p95 190ms, cost ~ $0.78 / 1M tokens, QA pass@1 77.1
int6: latency p95 160ms, cost ~ $0.44 / 1M tokens, QA pass@1 75.3
```

aj: So roughly int6 is ~44% cheaper than int8 and ~56% cheaper than fp16. Quality drop vs fp16 is ~3.1 pts pass@1 — which is noticeable but not catastrophic.

lucy: Does the QA drop correlate with specific prompt families or is it uniform? any calibration/priming fixes tried?

maya: Looks concentrated on multi-step reasoning prompts and long-chain context. short QA and retrievals are mostly fine. priming tweaks gave small lift (~0.4 pts), but didn't close the gap.

chris: Two practical questions: 1) product impact — what % of traffic is sensitive to that ~3 pt drop? 2) can we route high-value queries to int8/fp16 automatically?

maya: From gtn sample: ~18% of calls are labeled high-value (payments, legal, summary-of-record). Those are the ones where pass@1 matters most.

ravi: Routing is doable. Proposed policy: default -> int6, but route if (a) user flagged high-value OR (b) predicted difficulty score > 0.6 -> int8. fallback to fp16 on repeat failures. That would cover most risk.

aj: Metrics for rollout: keep unit-cost budget target and set quality guardrail triggers. e.g., if daily QA pass@1 for the high-value cohort drops >1.5 pts vs baseline for 3 consecutive days, rollback. Also track latency tail and error rate.

maya: Agree. Suggest initial canary: 5% overall traffic -> int6 baseline with routing enabled (high-value forced to int8). hold for 72h, collect slices and manual review.

ops-bot: deploy job queued: `deploy/canary/germanium-int6 @ 5%` (eta 15m) :rocket:

lucy: For GTN / product guidance: recommend adding a note that int6 is cost-optimal for high-volume UI features (autocomplete, search prompts) but not for safety/critical flows. include fallback and a short prompt-template to mitigate long-reasoning drift.

chris: Can we add a tiny eval harness to run nightly 2k examples on the high-value slice and produce automated diff report? I can wire up the pager alerts if regressions exceed threshold.

ravi: Yes — add `nightly-germanium-int6-highvalue` job, output to console + attach sample failures for triage. keep retention 30 days.

maya: Cool. I'll file a short runbook for oncall: rollout steps, rollback triggers, and where to find diffs. tagging @product for FYI.

aj: TL;DR recommendation: proceed with 5% canary int6 + routing to int8 for high-value + nightly eval + 1.5pt high-value guardrail. if pass, scale to 30% and re-evaluate before full rollout. :thumbsup:

maya: Thanks everyone — will start the canary and post updates here.
